Initial public release of **Citation Needed** (出处呢): what the research says about how software teams work.

**58 claims in nine chapters**: AI coding tools, measuring productivity, working hours, meetings and focus, remote work, estimation and project failure, engineering practices, team size and structure, hiring and performance. Each has a verdict, an A/B/C evidence grade, primary sources, what would change our mind, and one sentence you can say to your boss. English and 简体中文.

**In this release**

- `citation-needed-reader.html`: the web reader as one offline file (search, filter, build a one-page brief)
- `citation-needed-en.pdf`, `citation-needed-zh-CN.pdf`: the whole handbook as a book
- `claims.json`: all claims and sources as data
- `verification-report.json`: source-check results tied to the release commit
- `citation-needed-skill.zip`: an Agent Skill, so an AI assistant answers with the grade and the source
- `citation-needed-share-cards.zip`: one share image per claim, in both languages

**How it is checked.** The release workflow looks up every source online (Crossref, OpenAlex, Europe PMC, arXiv), compares metadata and matches registered quote snippets for sources marked for abstract verification. Sources marked metadata-only or link-only receive those narrower checks. The release gate requires every result to be OK, with no warnings or failures. Full-text figures, numerical context, causal interpretations and evidence grades are not machine-validated. This is an evidence handbook for discussion, not a certification that all conclusions are proven. The text was drafted with AI assistance and has not had a line-by-line expert review. If you find a mistake, open a Challenge issue; grades move in public.
